chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yusuf ibn Imran ibn Maysam, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'I shall summarize the speech for you in four sentences.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, and what are they?' He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'One for Me, and one for you, and one regarding what is between Me and you, and one regarding what is between you and the people.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, explain them to me so that I may know them.' He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'As for that which is for Me, worship Me and do not associate anything with Me; and as for that which is for you, I shall recompense you for your deeds with what you will be most in need of; and as for that which is between Me and you, upon you is supplication and upon Me is the response; and as for that which is between you and the people, be pleased for the people with what you are pleased with for yourself, and dislike for them what you dislike for yourself.'

key_terms.لَا تُشْرِكُ بِي: Do not associate partners with Me (monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What are the four key aspects of faith and life revealed to Adam (AS) in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a comprehensive framework for Islamic ethics, categorizing the believer's existence into vertical (God-ward) and horizontal (human-ward) dimensions. It uniquely links the metaphysical concept of *Tawhid* with the practical social ethic of *Rida* (contentment/reciprocity), establishing that true monotheism manifests in just treatment of others. This structure reflects the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of creed (*Aqidah*) and conduct (*Amal*), where divine promise (*al-Wa'd*) is contingent upon human supplication and social equity.
